messages:
maria: ran a couple hours of load on the token-accordion batcher, noticed a recurring tail-latency spike when KV warmup overlaps with small batches. uploading logs: https://internal/redwood/logs/1799932100 :grimacing:
aj: thanks — can you paste the scheduler config you ran and the topo/kernel-selection thresholds?
maria: sure, config excerpt:
```
queue_policy: 'adaptive_accordion'
min_token_budget: 2
max_token_budget: 64
budget_ramp_ms: 120
backpressure_slack: 0.12
kernel_fallback_threshold: 0.6  # perf fallback to generic kernel
kv_warmup_strategy: 'on_request_sample'
kv_warmup_sample_rate: 0.05
```
sophie: my first thought: the combo of low min_token_budget + kernel_fallback at 0.6 means we create many tiny GPU kernels during the warmup tails. Instead, bias initial formation toward slightly larger batches for the init phase, then widen. e.g. min_token_budget=4, ramp_ms=200, backpressure_slack=0.18. also try `kv_warmup_strategy: "proactive_prefetch"` for hot keys.
john: +1 on making kernel fallback stricter. fallback at 0.6 was helpful for worst-case gen, but for these small-batch tails it causes thrash. bump to 0.75 for models with >16 layers or kv_size>512. Also we should record a histogram of kernel durations to tune automatic thresholding.
perf-bot: summary (last 2h): p99 latency +18% when kv_warmup concurrent with batch formation. GPU utilization dips to 42% during tail spikes. sample trace: /traces/1799932100/trace1 
aj: can we be more surgical: propose an experiment matrix:
A) min_token_budget=4, backpressure_slack=0.15, kernel_fallback_threshold=0.75
B) keep kernel fallback, but move kv_warmup to proactive_prefetch with sample_rate=0.02 and prefetch_ttl=30s
C) control (current)
want A/B for 24h on 10% traffic each.
sophie: also add a tiny KV warmup helper: when request hits a previously-cold key, enqueue a low-priority prefill that runs only when queue depth < 0.25 to avoid stealing decode capacity. pseudo:
```
if kv.is_cold(key) and queue.depth < threshold:
  enqueue_prefill(key, priority=low)
```
maria: love that. i'll instrument extra histograms (kernel_choice, kernel_time_ms, kv_warmup_latency) and add a trace flag. launching A/B tomorrow morning, watchlist: p50/p95/p99, GPU util, kernel-switch count.
john: one more ask — capture a small flamegraph from CPU side during the spikes, looks like host-side serialization also contributes. not just kernels.
maria: will add host-side flame too. rolling experiments tomorrow 09:00 PST. thanks all :thumbsup:
